about: A split: u1 and u2 share one Brain Dump source line. u1 (to idea-mara) is approved on round 0; u2 (to idea-tobias) gets a fix on rounds 0, 1 and 2 and is undone, its copy leaving idea-tobias. `pointers` writes u1's pointer only, and it stays on the line. The Edit guard gives [] and the run closes with no second check. The shared source line stays off the handled list, so the next run retries u2; u1's copy still goes on as `written`, and nothing of u2's copy goes on. The log opens with 'Nothing needs you.' (no questions) and lists u1 under Migrated, then u2 under Units undone (the line quoted, idea-tobias, round 2's problem, then 'The next migration run tries this again.').
spec: CONTRACT.md 5.6 item 3 ('A source line shared by a counted unit and an undone unit stays off, so the next run retries the undone unit ... The counted unit's copies still go on as `written`'), item 6; spec-run-manager.md 11 Decisions Log items 81, 83 (supersedes item 79)
readings: New handled entries follow the ones already there, sorted by note path (as Python sorts strings, so 'Ideas/…' comes before 'brain-dump.md'), then by their place in the note at close. Neither spec nor contract fixes the order, and run-state.json is compared as parsed JSON, so list order counts.
A handled entry's `pointer` lists every destination on the line at close, as paths inside the project.

The line stays off with u1's pointer on it. The next run's scan matches it to no handled entry by text, and finds no handled entry in brain-dump.md with that pointer whose text has gone (CONTRACT.md 5.2 item 8), so it is new work, and 'The next migration run tries this again.' holds. The migrator's instruction 5 keeps u1's copy from being written twice.
